skill.description: Guides JavaScript and TypeScript developers through Azure Blob authentication, container management, transfers, metadata, SAS tokens, and SDK error handling.

security_audit.summary: All 102 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown, TypeScript templates, expected Azure endpoints, named environment variables, and a placeholder file stream. One medium issue remains because the container and account SAS examples grant broad permissions for 24 hours.

remediation.issue: The container and account SAS examples grant broader permissions and longer access than many tasks require.
remediation.suggestion: Use task-specific permissions, shorter expirations, user delegation SAS, and guidance for secure delivery and revocation.

content.user_title: Build Azure Blob Storage Workflows in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure Blob Storage code requires careful authentication, transfer, and permission choices. This skill provides focused TypeScript and JavaScript patterns for common SDK workflows.
actual_capabilities: Configure BlobServiceClient with DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, shared keys, or SAS tokens.
Create, list, and delete containers using Azure Storage client methods.
Upload and download blobs from strings, buffers, files, streams, and browser data.
List, copy, delete, and inspect blobs, properties, metadata, and HTTP headers.
Generate blob, container, and account SAS tokens with configurable permissions and expiry.
Handle block, append, and page blobs with TypeScript SDK examples.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples; it does not execute Azure operations or verify credentials.
Requires Node.js 18 or newer for the documented SDK version and Node-specific methods.
Browser support excludes shared-key authentication, file streams, direct file downloads, and SAS generation.
Examples use placeholder resources and require permission, security, and error-handling review before production use.

use_cases.title: Build a backend storage service
use_cases.description: Implement authenticated blob uploads, downloads, listing, metadata updates, and error handling in a Node.js service.

use_cases.title: Prepare secure browser uploads
use_cases.description: Design browser uploads with short-lived SAS access and uploadData without exposing storage account keys.

use_cases.title: Automate storage maintenance
use_cases.description: Create maintenance utilities for containers, blob copies, file transfers, and narrowly scoped SAS generation.

prompt_templates.title: Connect with managed identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal TypeScript example that connects to [ACCOUNT_NAME] with DefaultAzureCredential and lists containers. Include required packages and basic error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a file transfer flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js TypeScript service that uploads [LOCAL_PATH] to [CONTAINER]/[BLOB_NAME] and downloads it to [DESTINATION]. Stream large files and report progress.

prompt_templates.title: Design a browser upload
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a browser upload flow for [FILE_TYPE] using a server-issued, short-lived SAS token. Restrict permissions and validate size, type, and destination.
prompt_templates.scenario: Direct client upload with limited access

prompt_templates.title: Harden a storage pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Blob workflow for concurrency, retries, idempotency, conditional writes, observability, and least privilege. Propose production changes and tests.

output_examples.input: Show me how to upload a PDF from Node.js with managed identity.
output: Authentication: use DefaultAzureCredential with the storage account endpoint.
Transfer: upload the local PDF and set the application/pdf content type.
Checks: verify access, report progress, and handle authorization or conflict errors.

output_examples.input: Review a browser upload SAS that grants write and delete access for one day.
output: Risk: delete permission and a one-day lifetime exceed the upload requirement.
Recommendation: allow only required actions, use a short expiry, and restrict the destination.
Operations: keep account keys on the server and never log the issued token.

output_examples.input: Explain why a container creation request returns status 409.
output: Cause: the container probably exists or conflicts with another operation.
Response: use createIfNotExists for idempotent setup and preserve unexpected error details.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential and managed identities instead of connection strings or account keys.
Grant only required SAS permissions, use short expirations, and keep tokens out of logs.
Stream large files, report progress, and handle retries and service errors explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not embed account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens in source code.
Do not issue broad, long-lived SAS tokens when a narrow token satisfies the operation.
Do not buffer very large blobs when streaming methods are available.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Azure operations?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Generated code still needs credentials, permissions, testing, and an Azure environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity. Use connection strings, account keys, or SAS only when deployment constraints require them.

faq.question: Can I use these examples in a browser?
faq.answer: Browser clients support uploadData and SAS access. Shared keys, file streams, direct file downloads, and SAS generation require Node.js.

faq.question: How should I transfer large files?
faq.answer: Use uploadStream, uploadFile, or downloadToFile where supported. Configure concurrency, progress reporting, retries, and memory limits for the workload.

faq.question: How can I secure SAS tokens?
faq.answer: Use minimal permissions, short expirations, HTTPS, restricted destinations, and server-side issuance. Never log tokens or expose account keys.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Add validation, retries, observability, conditional requests, least-privilege roles, and tests for your environment.
